verdict.rationale: Glama documents that developers can search its catalog and "inspect their capabilities." Its hosted no-login Inspector shows a server's available capabilities and tools over Streamable HTTP/SSE before you wire it into a client. However, the evidence does not explicitly show that listing pages expose per-tool input schemas, the transport type, or hosting attributes as inspectable metadata, and the Inspector itself requires a live connection. missing for 10: documented per-tool input schema display on server listings, explicit transport and hosting-attribute fields on listings, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can inspect a listed server's tools, input schemas, transport, and hosting attributes before connecting to it

citations.quote: Search Glama's curated catalog of open-source servers and remote connectors, inspect their capabilities
Glama's hosted inspector connects to remote Streamable HTTP and SSE endpoints so you can inspect available capabilities and test requests interactively
Inspect any MCP server directly from your browser. No login required.
